links.comparator_used: Federated updates without Secure Aggregation (plain FL, attacked by FedMIA)
links.outcome: Membership inference attack discrimination (AUC) and synthesis quality
links.effect: FedMIA AUC 0.92-0.99 without SecAgg; with SecAgg AUC fell to 0.23-0.56 across all centers, with no impact on synthesis quality
links.quote: The introduction of SecAgg reduced AUC values to near-random levels (0.23-0.56) across all centers without impacting synthesis quality.

links.outcome: Model performance under data poisoning (noise injection) relative to the no-poisoning baseline
links.effect: High-noise poisoning: FedAvg rendered the federation inoperative, while FedMedian restored performance close to baseline in most scenarios. Low noise: FedMedian's advantage was less consistent.
links.tradeoff: Significant residual degradation remained in specific center configurations. Low-level noise may be indistinguishable from natural heterogeneity across centers, potentially enabling stealthy degradation.
links.quote: Under high-noise poisoning, the standard federated averaging (FedAvg) aggregation rendered the federation inoperative, while FedMedian restored performance close to the no-poisoning baseline in most scenarios, with significant residual degradation in specific center configurations.

design_hint: Secure aggregation and Byzantine-robust median aggregation as federated learning security safeguards
